$comment: Shared contract between the editor's C# checker and the browser checker (pdf.js). Authoritative copy: testdata/redaction-corpus/redaction-check-spec.json in the abyo PDF Editor repository; the browser checker mirrors it. Both implementations load THIS file for thresholds; neither hard-codes a number. Changing any value or rule bumps specVersion. Version 1 agreed 2026-10-20; version 1.1 agreed 2026-10-20 after the browser checker found false passes (see changes and requirements); version 1.2 agreed 2026-10-20 (annotation flags, word-boundary visible text, A7 recovered words, noteKey earlier-revision-not-read, detail as a code, declared evidence values, dictionary-drawn annotations; #115-#122); version 1.3 agreed 2026-10-20 (closed subpaths measured separately, strokes as per-segment ribbons, A3 takes any dark cover of an annotation, a clip kept as its pieces, every emitted code reached; #123-#134); version 1.4 agreed 2026-10-20 (winding-aware holes, the A3 ladder's two thresholds, coverage against the union of the covers, clip pieces as regions, limits that never reduce what is reported, form values read rather than counted, and the unit of findings outside the contract, the recovered span; #135-#146); version 1.5 opened 2026-10-20 (fixtures found by mutation testing, A9 tooltips, link targets, annotation authors, rich text and subjects, the Off rule for buttons only, remedy text with every new report, clip pieces as regions a MUST, unknown glyphs stay covered, inline image decoding; #147-#158). See docs/design/disclosure-redaction/design.md sections 4.2.1 and 8.

1.5: clip pieces as regions (MUST, was SHOULD in 1.4): when a clip piece is used for glyph visibility (A4 outside-clip), the piece MUST be the region its subpath encloses, never that subpath's bounding box. The bounding box of a triangle (#150) or of a rectangle turned by a rotation (#153, what a landscape scan placed by a rotation makes) adds corners where nothing is drawn, and text there was taken as drawn: a false pass. #153 discriminates for an implementation that tests glyph by glyph (#150's line also runs past its box, so such an implementation reports it either way). #151 and #154 are the guards (text the clip keeps is not reported)

glyphBox (coverage of an unknown glyph): a glyph never drops out of coverage because its character is unknown or unmappable; only a glyph that maps to white space may be ignored. A font with /Differences glyph names and no /ToUnicode under a black bar is covered text (#158), whatever an extractor makes of the names

imageDecoding (inline images): an inline image's samples are read like an image XObject's, its /Decode (/D) applied. A /Decode [1 0] image of 255s is black and is a dark cover (#155); without /Decode the same samples are white, an opaque cover that is not dark (#156, review)

A9 annotationText and annotationAuthors: an annotation's /RC (rich text) and /Subj count as annotation text whatever the subtype, like /Contents. A markup annotation's /T is its author, a person's name, and counts as its own kind (annotationAuthors); a widget's /T is its field name and is not an author. /Subj is OPTIONAL to list, because pdf.js does not expose it; an implementation that lists it conforms (#152)

A9 formValues (Off): only the NAME /Off on a button field (/FT /Btn, inherited through /Parent) is the unset state and not a value. The STRING (Off), and any value of a field that is not a button, is something somebody typed and counts (#157)
remedy text: when a check learns to report something new, its remedy text is part of the change (verdicts.wordingRules). A9's remedy names every kind it lists, bookmark titles and XMP explicitly

A9 tooltips and linkTargets: two more kinds A9 lists (kind codes tooltips and linkTargets). A form field's /TU always counts; a link's /URI counts only when it is mailto:, carries user information or carries a query string, so a plain web address is not listed. As for every A9 kind, the values are for the screen (recovered) and the saved report keeps the kind and the count

fixtures found by mutation testing: a mutation that leaves every corpus case passing marks arithmetic no file exercises. #147 puts every glyph of a line under two dark bars whose union leaves a band showing (A2, mustNotFlag A1: an exact union that reported everything as fully covered passed every earlier case); #148 draws a black bar under a matrix rotated twelve degrees (the first cover whose transform is neither a translation nor a scale); #149 places a black image by such a matrix, so deciding whether its pixels are dark under a glyph needs the inverse with its cross terms. No rule changes with them: they hold rules already stated (glyphBox.coverage, candidate.rectangularity, the image cover of candidate)
1.4: candidate.region (hole rule, restated): whether a nested subpath is a hole is decided by the fill rule on the actual winding numbers, never by nesting alone. Under even-odd a point is painted when it is enclosed an odd number of times. Under nonzero it is painted when the sum of the windings around it (each subpath's orientation, read from the sign of its area) is not zero: an inner subpath wound against its outer is a hole (#135 under even-odd, guarded by #136 with the text on the band), one wound the same way is not, and the shape is solid (#137). An implementation that treats any nesting as a hole calls text inside a solid shape visible

A3 ladder (reminder): the ladder has two thresholds. A dark appearance fails from coverPartialMin; an appearance that is only opaque is a review only from coverFail. Applying coverPartialMin to every opaque appearance reports an ordinary pale box that merely touches a line. coveredFraction remains per glyph box (coveredFraction(glyphBox, candidate)), so a pale box that hides the first glyphs of a line whole is the middle rung, a review (#138); measuring over the whole line would let a grey box over one name in a sentence pass

glyphBox.coverage: a glyph's coveredFraction is measured against the UNION of all the dark covers drawn after it, not cover by cover (no maximum over single covers, no sum). Two bars meeting on a seam through a glyph cover it fully, an A1 and not a partial cover (A2) by each (#139); ten narrow abutting bars, each covering a tenth of a line, hide all of it (#140). The same holds wherever a check compares coveredFraction with a threshold for dark covers: A1, A2, A5, and the dark covers of one annotation's appearance for A3. Non-dark and unread-colour covers are still measured one at a time

clip pieces as regions: when a clip piece is used for glyph visibility (A4 outside-clip), the piece SHOULD be the region its subpath encloses, not that subpath's bounding box. A bounding box is larger than a rotated or non-rectangular piece, so text in the corner it adds is taken as drawn: a narrow miss, hence SHOULD and not MUST

limits: a cap or limit inside an implementation must never reduce what is reported. Exceeding it either over-states coverage, or marks the page as not fully examined (the reviewFloor, with a declared checksSkipped reason or noteKey). It never falls back to an approximation that can hide text. A clip kept as the hull of its pieces once their number passed a cap made the gaps between the pieces part of the clip, and text in a gap passed with no finding (#144: a name in the gap between two bands of eighty clip pieces, inside their hull)

A9 formValues: a form value is what a terminal field's /V holds, read from the field tree and from widget annotations: a text string (#141), a name, or an ARRAY of strings or names (a multi-select choice, #142). A field that exists without a value, an empty string, and the name Off on a button field (a check box or radio button that is not set; 1.5: the string (Off), or Off on a field that is not a button, IS a value, #157) are not values; counting the fields that exist reports values on a blank form (#143)
findings: the number of findings and their unit (one per cover, per run or per glyph) are NOT part of the contract. What a manifest case states - the verdict, the required checks and mustNotFlag - is

recovered span: the recovered text of a cover finding (A1, A2, A3, A5) is, for each line, the span from the first covered character to the last, read back from the run so that its spaces survive - including a gap written as a move rather than a space glyph: "amada Taro of Yoko", not "amadaTaroofYoko". Never the whole run: the uncovered words around the span are still printed on the page and are not recovered from under anything (#145, #146)

what the manifest constrains: the verdict and which checks fire (expect.checks, mustNotFlag). What a finding says - its recovered text, its evidence - is constrained by each implementation's own tests
1.3: candidate.rectangularity / candidate.region: a filled path is measured one closed subpath at a time. Each subpath is its own painted region with its own rectangularity, so two bars painted by one fill operator are two covers (#123), not one hull about 5% filled. A subpath nested inside another is a hole when the fill rule leaves its inside unpainted (even-odd, or nonzero with the windings cancelling): the outer then covers only the ring around the hole, never the hole. Subpaths that overlap without nesting are each taken as painted throughout (an over-estimate, the safe direction for A1). Subpaths that touch and together are rectangular may be measured as one region, so a glyph on the seam between two abutting bars is not split between them

candidate.strokedPath: a stroke paints a ribbon along each segment of each subpath (the closing segment included for a closed subpath), each the segment grown by half the line width, never the area the path encloses. A frame drawn after text is not a cover of the text inside it (#124), and a frame drawn before text is not the background that text is read against (A4, #125). A fill-and-stroke (B, B*, b, b*) is its fill regions and then its ribbons, so a white box with a black border over text is still an opaque non-dark cover (#126)

A3: every cover an annotation's appearance paints is considered, not the first in draw order. The annotation fails when any dark cover covers text with coveredFraction >= coverPartialMin; otherwise it is a review when a non-dark opaque cover covers text with coveredFraction >= coverFail. Still one finding per annotation (#127)

clip: W and W* mark the path that the NEXT painting operator (n, f, S, ...) ends; that path, not an earlier one, becomes the clip when it is painted (ISO 32000-1 8.5.4). An implementation that applies W to the path before it applies no clip at all (#128)

clip: a clip is kept as its pieces - the regions its closed subpaths enclose under W's fill rule (nonzero for W, even-odd for W*), each measured as candidate.rectangularity measures a fill - intersected piece by piece with the clip in force. A glyph is outside the clip (A4) when its box meets none of the pieces: the hull of two clip rectangles covers the gap between them and would call text in the gap visible (#129); text inside a piece is not reported (#130)

clip: a paint's effective region is the paint intersected with each clip piece, so a bar clipped to half a name covers half of it, an A2 and not an A1 (#131). An implementation may trim covers by the clip's hull instead (an over-estimate of the cover, the safe direction for A1/A2), but MUST test glyph visibility against the pieces

reachability: every finding detail, noteKey and checksSkipped reason an implementation can emit is reached by at least one corpus file or by a named rule test, or is declared unreached with a written reason. #132 (an undecodable image as the cover, A1 checksSkipped image-pixels-not-readable), #133 (a dark bar over an undecodable image, A6) and #134 (#111 with its /Prev broken too) were added because no file reached those branches

A9 documentInfo on a repaired file: when the document opens only through a repair (a broken /Prev), the document information the LAST trailer names is read from the bytes as well; a repair that takes another trailer must not lose it (#134)
1.2: drawOrder.annotationFlags: Hidden (/F bit 2) is not drawn and is not a cover (#116); NoView (bit 6) is still a cover, because it covers on paper; Print (bit 3) clear is still a cover, because it covers on screen; /Redact is A3 whatever its flags

visibleText: one normative visible-text filter for A7 and A8. Words are matched on word boundaries against the visible text with its white space kept (a glyph gap or a line change separates text); a hidden 'Li' is not visible inside a printed 'Click' or 'Lions' (#117). The white-space-insensitive comparison of 1.1 remains only as a fallback for a string of several words broken by a re-flow (#114), never for a single word

A7: words are the letter-or-digit runs of each white-space-separated string; only hidden words are recovered, and a string all of whose words are hidden is recovered as written, so a date stays one string (#115)
A7: outcome 3 (and the chain floor's finding) carries noteKey earlier-revision-not-read
finding.noteKey: earlier-revision-not-read; read-from-file-bytes names A7 as well as A8

finding.detail: a code matching ^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$ (page-not-examined: the failure name), never document text; string evidence values are codes or standard PDF names, and an annotation subtype outside the standard list is written as other. The saved report is byte-identical whether or not findings carry recovered text

finding.detail / finding.evidence: the failure name of a page-not-examined finding (a library's error type name) may be carried in detail or in evidence.failure; both conform, and a comparison of two reports never depends on which

finding.evidence: every string evidence key has declared values, a closed set of codes and standard PDF names or the kind failure name; a value outside its key's declaration, or a string key with no declaration, is non-conformant. checksSkipped detail likewise: an image filter ISO 32000 does not define is written as other, never the document's spelling
visibleText.lineChange: a separation taken from an extractor must survive a line change (#118, a word at the start of a line joined to the line before it)
drawOrder.annotationFlags: a Hidden /Redact is still A3 (#119)

annotationAppearance.withoutAppearance: only Square, Circle and Highlight are drawn from the dictionary; any other subtype with no usable appearance, standard (#122) or unknown (#121), draws nothing and is not a cover. An unknown subtype WITH an appearance is judged by what it paints, like any other (#120)
1.1: requirements: four normative requirements (formXObject, annotationAppearance, shading, strokeState), each with a corpus fixture (#99-#103); an implementation that misses one passes a leaking file
checksSemantics: implementations agree on the VERDICT; expect.checks is a required subset, extra checks are allowed except those in mustNotFlag
A3: the ladder (/Redact or a dark appearance -> fail; opaque but light -> review; a /Highlight that is not dark -> no finding)
A9: which document-information entries count, in PDF terms; annotation /Contents is listed explicitly (#107)

A10: coverage is the SUM of the areas of the page's image paints, each after CTM and clip and intersected with the CropBox, over the CropBox area, capped at 1 (v1: one image). Not their union bounding box: two small images in opposite corners would span the page (#106)
A11: fires only when the file cannot be opened; owner-password-only files are examined and pass A11
glyphBox.vertical: the box for vertical writing mode
units.luminance: annotation colour arrays and Lab
fileReport.notInspected: fixed keys instead of sentences
candidate.sources: shading
type3Glyphs: expanding Type 3 glyph procedures is RECOMMENDED; an implementation that cannot must report type3-glyph-not-inspected and never pass the file (#104)

checksSkipped: reasons are fixed codes (reasonCodes); page, count and detail are separate fields, never interpolated. image-codec-not-decodable:<Filter> became image-pixels-not-readable with detail = the filter
finding.noteKey: a fixed code when a finding says something could not be examined; such a finding is not rendered with the check's generic description and remedy
verdicts.wording.passWithSkipped: the pass headline is qualified whenever checksSkipped is non-empty

checksSkipped: reason check-failed (page, detail = the failure name) for an internal failure while examining a page; the other pages are still examined, and the page carries a review finding with noteKey page-not-examined, so the file is never pass (verdicts.reviewFloor)
finding.noteKey: page-not-examined

A7: earlier revisions are found by the cross-reference chain AND by surplus %%EOF markers (revisionDiscovery, #108, #109); three outcomes (fail / nothing / review), and 'all recovered text is visible' needs something read (#110, #111)
checksSkipped: reason revisions-not-readable for A7, detail chain or revision, with its floor in verdicts.reviewFloor
verdicts.reviewFloor: page-level failures are carried on A1 and mean that none of the page-level checks ran on that page
manifest.sharedExpectations: where shared expectations stop

A7/A8/A9 onOpenFailure: when the file cannot be opened, A7, A8 and A9 run from the file's bytes; A7 and A8 are review there (noteKey read-from-file-bytes); A9 lists document information, attachments and JavaScript; they are in checksRun, not checksSkipped (#112, #113)
finding.noteKey: read-from-file-bytes
A7/A8 visible-text filter: the comparison ignores white space on both sides (#114)

units.length: PDF points in the page's user space after CTM and clipping, before /Rotate; origin bottom-left (rect = x0,y0,x1,y1 with x0<x1, y0<y1)
units.luminance: L = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on 0..1 components as written in the PDF (no gamma decoding). DeviceGray g -> R=G=B=g. DeviceCMYK -> R=(1-C)(1-K), G=(1-M)(1-K), B=(1-Y)(1-K). ICCBased/CalRGB: use the alternate/N-component rule above. Lab: L = L*/100 (a* and b* ignored). Indexed: look up the base. Separation/DeviceN: tint transform when available, else unknown: never a dark candidate, and a cover of unknown colour is graded like requirements.shading (review, noteKey fill-colour-unreadable). An annotation colour array (/C, /IC) is read by its length (1 gray, 3 RGB, 4 CMYK, 0 = transparent) with every component normalised to 0..1 before the formula (clamped; an implementation whose library returns 0..255 divides by 255 first).

checksSemantics.verdict: Two implementations, and an implementation and the manifest, must agree on the file VERDICT (fail/review/pass).
checksSemantics.checks: expect.checks is a REQUIRED SUBSET: every listed check must be raised; checks not listed may also be raised, except those in expect.mustNotFlag, whose appearance is a false positive.
checksSemantics.annotationCovers: A cover drawn by an annotation appearance must raise A3. An implementation MAY also raise A1 for it (the browser checker does, the editor does not); a manifest lists only A3 for such a cover.
checksSemantics.$comment: Agreed 2026-10-20 (v1.1). Rect and per-finding detail are not part of the contract; a differential run compares verdict, the raised-check set within these rules, and page numbers.

verdicts.fileVerdict: worst finding verdict; pass when there are no findings. A check listed in checksSkipped never yields pass for that check (the one exception is revisions-not-readable with detail chain, see reviewFloor); the report must show it.
verdicts.reviewFloor: A file that was not completely examined is never pass: the verdict is at least review. In particular a page with checksSkipped reason check-failed carries an A1 finding with verdict review, the page, noteKey page-not-examined and detail = the failure name; findings already made on that page and on every other page are kept, and the remaining pages and the document checks are still examined (a file that leaks on page 1 and fails internally on page 3 still reports the page-1 fail). A7: revisions-not-readable with detail revision (an earlier revision exists and nothing legible could be read from it) always floors the verdict at review, with an A7 review finding; detail chain (the cross-reference chain cannot be followed, or a byte prefix found by an %%EOF marker does not open) floors it at review ONLY when nothing at all could be read from the earlier bytes - when another earlier revision was read, the entry is listed and the pass headline is qualified (wording.passWithSkipped), but no finding is added.
verdicts.pageLevelCarrier: page-not-examined and type3-not-inspected findings, and their checksSkipped entries (check-failed, type3-glyph-not-inspected), are carried on A1 by convention. A1 is only the carrier: a page that could not be examined means that NONE of the page-level checks (A1-A6, A10) ran on that page. An implementation MUST NOT list every page-level check for a failed page, and the reader-facing sentence describes the page, not the check.

wording.pass: 検査した{n}項目で問題は見つかりませんでした
wording.passWithSkipped: 検査した{n}項目で問題は見つかりませんでした。ただし、文書の一部で実行できなかった検査があります

wordingRules: When checksSkipped is non-empty, an implementation MUST NOT present the pass headline as 'n checks found nothing' without qualification; it uses passWithSkipped, which states that some checks could not run on part of the document.

A finding that carries a noteKey says the implementation could not examine something; it MUST NOT be rendered with the check's generic description and remedy (which would claim a problem was found) - each surface shows its own sentence for the noteKey.
Neither checksSkipped reasons nor noteKeys are ever shown as raw codes or extended with text; every surface owns the sentence for each code.

When a check learns to report something new, its remedy text is part of the change (1.5): the remedy a finding shows names what the reader is looking at and what removes it, in every shipped language. For A9 that means every kind it lists, including the two the usual advice misses: bookmark titles, which clearing the document information does not touch, and XMP metadata, a store separate from the document properties that many tools leave behind when the properties are cleared. How an implementation checks this is its own (this one declares the words each kind's remedy must contain and fails a build in which a kind it can emit lacks them).

drawOrder.rule: Page content stream(s) in order, with every Form XObject expanded at its Do (recursively, including nested forms, patterns are NOT expanded) under requirements.formXObject, then each annotation's normal appearance (/AP /N, honouring /F under annotationFlags and /OC off) in /Annots order, placed under requirements.annotationAppearance. Annotations are always above page content.
drawOrder.annotationFlags: v1.2. The check asks whether an annotation covers text on screen OR on paper. Hidden (/F bit 2, value 2): drawn nowhere, so it is not a cover and raises no A1, A2 or A3 (#116); Hidden wins over every other flag. NoView (bit 6, value 32): not shown on screen but printed, so it is still a cover - a printed copy shows the box while the text under it can be extracted. Print (bit 3, value 4) clear: shown on screen but not printed, so it is still a cover. Invisible (bit 1) concerns only annotation types a viewer does not know and is not read. A /Redact annotation is reported by A3 whatever its flags (an unapplied redaction mark, regardless of what it draws).

requirements.$comment: Normative since v1.1. Each one is a way an implementation reported a file with readable text under an opaque cover as clean; the fixture named is the case that goes wrong without it.

formXObject.rule: Everything drawn inside a Form XObject is transformed by the form's /Matrix (concatenated onto the CTM at the Do) and clipped by the form's /BBox mapped through that matrix. A cover placed only by the form matrix is a cover where the matrix puts it.

annotationAppearance.rule: An annotation's appearance stream is fitted to /Rect per PDF 32000-1 12.5.5 (Algorithm 8.1): transform the appearance /BBox by its /Matrix, take the bounding box of the result, and map that box onto /Rect (scale and translate); the appearance's content is drawn through /Matrix then that mapping, clipped to /Rect. The colour comes from the appearance stream, not from /C or /IC.
annotationAppearance.withoutAppearance: An annotation with no usable /AP /N is drawn from /IC, else /C (units.luminance for the array): a Square fills its /Rect, a Circle the ellipse inscribed in /Rect, a Highlight its /QuadPoints quads (none -> nothing drawn) with blend mode Multiply; /CA is the alpha. No colour -> nothing drawn. /Redact is A3 regardless of what it draws. v1.2: ONLY these three subtypes are drawn from the dictionary, because only for them does a viewer synthesise an appearance from /IC or /C; an annotation of any other subtype with no usable /AP /N draws nothing and is not a cover, whether its subtype is a standard one (a Stamp with a black /IC, #122) or one ISO 32000 does not define (#121). An annotation of an unknown subtype that HAS an appearance is drawn like any other and judged by what it paints (A3, #120).

shading.rule: A shading - the sh operator, which paints the current clip (the whole page when unclipped), or a fill or stroke whose colour is a pattern (shading or tiling) - is a cover whose colour cannot be read from the content stream. When it is opaque and cover-shaped (candidate.opaque and candidate.size on its effective region) and covers earlier text with coveredFraction >= coverFail, it is an unreadable cover: an A1 finding with verdict below and noteKey fill-colour-unreadable - never fail, never silently ignored. The check did run, so this is a finding, not a checksSkipped entry.

strokeState.rule: Stroke colour (G, RG, K, CS/SC/SCN) and stroke alpha (CA, including CA set through an ExtGState with gs) are tracked separately from the fill colour and fill alpha (g, rg, k, cs/sc/scn, ca). A stroked path is graded by the stroke colour and stroke alpha only; a filled path by the fill state only.

limits.rule: A cap or limit inside an implementation must never reduce what is reported. Exceeding it either over-states coverage, or marks the page as not fully examined (verdicts.reviewFloor, with a declared checksSkipped reason or noteKey). It never falls back to an approximation that can hide text (1.4)

visibleText.rule: v1.2. Whether a string is shown in the current document (A7's words, A8's replacement texts). The visible text is the extracted text of the page (A8) or of every page (A7) with white space kept, and with a separator between two consecutive glyphs that are not adjacent: on another line, or with a gap along the line wider than wordGapEm times the font size (a word gap written as a TJ adjustment or a move instead of a space). A word is shown when it occurs in the visible text on word boundaries: the character before the match and the character after it are each absent, not a letter or digit, or (with the neighbouring matched character) a CJK ideograph or kana, scripts written without spaces. A word is never shown by the inside of a longer word: a hidden 'Li' is not shown by a printed 'Click' or 'Lions' (#117).
visibleText.multiWord: A string of several words is shown when it occurs, each run of white space matching any run of white space, on word boundaries; failing that, when its characters without white space occur in the visible text without white space, and the match begins and ends on word boundaries of the visible text (a re-flow that split the string across lines or runs, #114). This white-space-insensitive fallback is NEVER used for a single word: a word split by a separator is reported, which is a false alarm at worst, whereas joining words would let a short name hide in a longer one.
visibleText.lineChange: an implementation that takes word separation from its extractor must satisfy itself that the separation survives a line change; consulting both the run-joined and run-separated forms is one way.

type3Glyphs.rule: A Type 3 font's glyphs are drawn by its /CharProcs procedures, which may paint covers. Expanding them is RECOMMENDED: walk the procedure of each shown glyph through /FontMatrix, then the text rendering matrix ([Tfs*Th 0 0 Tfs 0 Trise] x Tm), then the CTM, using the font's /Resources (else the page's). After d1 the glyph is a stencil: its colour operators are ignored and it paints in the fill colour in force where the glyph is shown; after d0 the procedure sets its own colours. A glyph's own drawing never covers that glyph, nor is it the background A4 reads that glyph against.
type3Glyphs.notInspected: An implementation that cannot inspect a Type 3 glyph's drawing (it does not expand procedures, or a procedure cannot be read) MUST add checksSkipped {check:"A1", reason:"type3-glyph-not-inspected", page, count} and an A1 finding with verdict review and noteKey type3-not-inspected, and MUST NOT return pass for that file: the verdict is at least review.

candidate.$comment: A 'cover candidate' (黒塗り候補). Evaluated on the EFFECTIVE region: shape transformed by CTM and intersected with the current clip. A shading (requirements.shading) is a cover whose colour is unknown: never a dark candidate, always reported.

size.$comment: Agreed: short side >= 3pt and long side >= 6pt, no area rule. A single masked digit at 8pt is about 5x8pt and must qualify. Thin rules (< 3pt) stay excluded; draw order removes header bands and table fills.

rectangularity.$comment: Oriented (minimum-area) bounding box, so rotated rectangles qualify. Measured per closed subpath (1.3); a nested subpath the fill rule leaves unpainted is a hole, not part of the outer's cover

strokedPath.$comment: marker-style blackouts drawn with a thick stroke; region = a ribbon per segment (1.3), each segment grown by half the line width, closing segment included; never the area the path encloses

image.$comment: an image counts as a cover candidate over the area where >= 95% of its decoded pixels are dark. ImageMask: candidate when the fill colour is dark. An image whose codec the implementation cannot decode is NOT a candidate; see imageDecoding.

nonDarkOpaqueCover.$comment: An opaque NON-dark fill drawn over earlier text also hides it (white-box cover, grey redaction box). Reported as A1 review, not fail, to avoid failing Excel-style cell overflow.

glyphBox.rule: Horizontal writing: x from the glyph origin to origin + advance (Tw/Tc/Tz applied); y from baseline + descent to baseline + ascent with a FIXED ascent of 0.8 em and descent of -0.2 em; then transformed by Tm x CTM. Vertical writing: see vertical. Both implementations MUST use this box, not ink bounds, so coverage fractions agree.
glyphBox.unknownGlyph: A glyph never drops out of coverage because its character is unknown or unmappable; only a glyph that maps to white space may be ignored (1.5, #158).

vertical.appliesWhen: the font writes vertically: /WMode 1 in its CMap, or a predefined vertical CMap (a name ending in -V, e.g. Identity-V, UniJIS-UCS2-V)
vertical.rule: In text space at the glyph origin: across the line x0 = origin.x - halfWidthEm, x1 = origin.x + halfWidthEm (in em, times Tfs); along the line y1 = origin.y, y0 = origin.y - advance, where advance is the vertical displacement (1 em by the default /DW2, plus Tc and Tw); then transformed by Tm x CTM. The 0.8/-0.2 em pair does not apply.

glyphBox.$comment: FontDescriptor /Ascent and /Descent are deliberately NOT read: pdf.js and PDFium expose them differently and missing/zero values are common, so a fixed box is the only one both engines compute identically.
glyphBox.coverage: coveredFraction(glyphBox, covers) is the area of the glyph box inside the UNION of the covers' effective regions over the glyph box's area (1.4). For dark covers it is taken over every dark cover drawn after the glyph at once (for A3, the dark covers of the one annotation's appearance); a cover that is not dark is measured on its own

imageDecoding.rule: When an implementation cannot read an image's pixels (typically /DCTDecode, /JPXDecode, /JBIG2Decode or /CCITTFaxDecode, depending on the engine), every check that needs that image's pixels yields REVIEW for the affected region, never pass, and the report adds a checksSkipped entry with reason image-pixels-not-readable, the page, the count of such images, and detail = the terminal filter name when known.
imageDecoding.$comment: detail is the terminal filter name without the slash, e.g. DCTDecode (v1 put it in the reason as image-codec-not-decodable:<Filter>). v1.2: a filter name ISO 32000 does not define (Table 6, or an inline-image abbreviation of one, Table 92) is written as other, never the document's spelling; unreadable when the filter chain cannot be read. Such an image is also not a cover candidate (its darkness is unknown). Corpus cases whose verdict depends on this carry expect.acceptVerdicts.

checks.title: 不透明な図形・画像の下に取り出せるテキスト
checks.rule: glyph drawn before candidates with coveredFraction >= coverFail against the union of the dark candidates drawn after it (glyphBox.coverage, 1.4). An opaque non-dark cover gives review (candidate.nonDarkOpaqueCover); a cover of unreadable colour (requirements.shading) gives review with noteKey fill-colour-unreadable; an image whose pixels cannot be read gives review with checksSkipped image-pixels-not-readable (imageDecoding); unread content gives checksSkipped content-truncated; Type 3 glyphs not inspected give type3Glyphs.notInspected; an internal failure while examining a page gives checksSkipped check-failed and the page-not-examined finding (verdicts.reviewFloor).

checks.title: 黒塗りが文字に一部しかかかっていない
checks.rule: coverPartialMin <= coveredFraction < coverFail for a glyph drawn before dark candidates, coveredFraction taken against their union (glyphBox.coverage, 1.4)

checks.title: 未適用の /Redact、または注釈で隠している
checks.rule: Any /Redact annotation (regardless of what is under it). Otherwise an annotation appearance (requirements.annotationAppearance) that covers earlier text, graded by the ladder.

ladder.fail: /Redact; or an opaque DARK appearance (candidate.dark, any subtype, /Highlight included) covering text with coveredFraction >= coverPartialMin. Every cover of the annotation's appearance is considered (1.3): a dark one anywhere in it decides, even after a non-dark one drawn first
ladder.review: an opaque appearance that is NOT dark covering text with coveredFraction >= coverFail (nonDarkOpaqueCover applied to annotations)
ladder.none: a /Highlight whose appearance is not dark: a highlighter hides nothing

checks.title: 白文字・背景同色・ページ外・クリップ外の文字
checks.rule: text whose |L(text) - L(background)| < hiddenContrast, where background = colour painted at the glyph centre BEFORE the text (paper white when nothing): FAIL regardless of proximity. Glyph box outside the CropBox, or fully clipped out: FAIL when within nearCandidatePt of a candidate, else REVIEW. Tr 3 text is A5, not A4.
checks.imageBackground: when the topmost painter under the glyph centre is an image, background = mean luminance of the image pixels under the glyph box; if its pixels cannot be read: REVIEW plus checksSkipped {check:"A4", reason:"image-pixels-not-readable", page, count, detail} (see imageDecoding), never pass

checks.title: 黒塗りの下の不可視テキスト（Tr 3）
checks.rule: Tr 3 (or 7) glyph with coveredFraction >= coverPartialMin under a candidate (glyph box, not run origin)

checks.title: 画像の上に黒い図形を重ねただけ
checks.rule: image drawn, then a candidate over it, AND the decoded image pixels under the candidate are NOT dark (darkPixelFraction < candidate.image.minDarkPixelFraction). Pixels already dark = the image was really redacted (Acrobat / this editor) -> no finding. Image pixels not readable by the implementation: REVIEW plus checksSkipped {check:"A6", reason:"image-pixels-not-readable", page, count, detail} (see imageDecoding), never pass.

checks.title: 増分更新の旧版に別の内容
checks.rule: list the earlier revisions (revisionDiscovery); for each, extract its text per page. Three outcomes: (1) legible text recovered that the current document does not show: fail; (2) legible text recovered and ALL of it shown in the current document (an ordinary incremental save): nothing is reported; (3) an earlier revision exists and nothing legible could be read from it: review with checksSkipped revisions-not-readable, detail revision, and noteKey earlier-revision-not-read on the finding. Outcome 2 requires that something was read: 'every recovered word is visible' is vacuously true of an empty list, which is outcome 3. Text is compared as words (v1.2): the revision's text is split at white space into strings, each string into words (maximal runs of letters or digits), and each word is searched for under visibleText (word boundaries; a single word gets no white-space-insensitive fallback). Recovered text lists only the hidden words: a string all of whose words are hidden is recovered as written (a date such as 2001-02-03 stays one string, not three numbers); of a string with some words visible, only its hidden words. One name removed from a sentence is recovered alone, not with the words still printed around it (#115). Text that only re-flowed between two saves is visible (#114).
checks.revisionDiscovery: Walk startxref and each /Prev (a /Prev pointing forward is a linearized file's first-page section, not a revision). Then count the %%EOF markers: the chain accounts for one per revision, plus one extra for a linearized file (a /Linearized dictionary in the first 1024 bytes). A surplus, or a chain that cannot be followed, means earlier bytes the chain does not point at (#108): the file prefix ending at each %%EOF marker before the last is read as an earlier revision too. Such a prefix may be the document itself (a stray marker, #109), which outcome 2 then reports as nothing. A chain that cannot be followed, or a marker prefix that does not open, adds revisions-not-readable with detail chain (verdicts.reviewFloor).
checks.compressedRevisions: Whether an implementation can decompress an earlier revision is a capability: one that reads earlier revisions through a full parser decompresses them and reports nothing when all their text is visible (#111); one that cannot reports outcome 3 (review, revisions-not-readable/revision). A7 review means an earlier revision exists and could not be read, not that it is compressed.
checks.onOpenFailure: When the file cannot be opened (open-failed), A7 still runs: earlier revisions are found and read as usual, but with no current page the visible-text filter cannot run, so text recovered from an earlier revision is reported as REVIEW, never fail, with the recovered text shown, noteKey read-from-file-bytes and evidence source fileBytes. Outcome 3 (nothing legible read) is reported as usual.

checks.title: 構造ツリーの /ActualText・/Alt に黒塗り部分の文字
checks.rule: /ActualText, /Alt or /E on a struct element or BDC property list whose content (MCIDs, or the element's page area) intersects a candidate, OR whose string is not found in the page's extractable text while the page has candidates; else listed under A9 as review. Whether the string is in the page's text is decided by visibleText, as for A7 (v1.2: word boundaries; the white-space-insensitive fallback only for a string of several words)
checks.onOpenFailure: When the file cannot be opened (reason open-failed; never for an encrypted file, which is A11's), A8 still runs, from the file's bytes: every /ActualText, /Alt and /E string found in the objects - literal or hex, PDFDocEncoding or UTF-16BE (or UTF-8) with its byte order mark, a direct string or one an indirect reference names, and inside Flate-compressed object streams and content streams where they can be decompressed - is reported as an A8 finding with verdict REVIEW and noteKey read-from-file-bytes, never fail: with no page to compare against, a tagged string over a blackout cannot be told from a caption. These are not listed again under A9. An implementation that repairs the file and opens it (for example by rebuilding the cross-reference table, or by taking the file's only catalog when the trailer's /Root names a missing object) examines the repaired document like any other, so A8 may be fail there (#112).

checks.title: 文書情報・XMP・しおり・添付・フォーム値・ツールチップ・リンク先・注釈本文・非表示レイヤー・サムネイル
checks.rule: list every non-empty item with its content (for the screen only; the saved report keeps item kind and count, not the value)
checks.annotationText: Every annotation's non-empty /Contents counts, whatever the subtype and whether or not the annotation covers anything (#107). It travels with the file without being part of the page. 1.5: its /RC (rich text) and /Subj count the same way; /Subj is optional to list, because pdf.js does not expose it (#152).
checks.annotationAuthors: 1.5: a markup annotation's non-empty /T is its author, a person's name never drawn on the page, and counts (#152). A widget's /T is its field name and is not listed as an author.
checks.tooltips: Every non-empty /TU (a form field's tooltip, ISO 32000-1 Table 220) counts: on any node of the AcroForm field tree, terminal or not (/TU is not inherited, but the text is in the file wherever it sits), and on a widget annotation the field tree does not reach. It is text somebody wrote, shown only when the pointer rests on the field (1.5).
checks.linkTargets: The /URI of a URI action (ISO 32000-1 12.6.4.7) counts only when it is a mailto: address, carries user information in its authority (scheme://user@host, user:password@host), or carries a query string (a ? before any fragment). A plain address (https://host/path, a fragment) does not count: it is what a link is for, and listing it would make every document with a reference list a review. Every URI action the file holds is read - a link annotation's /A, a bookmark's /A, a widget's or a page's /AA, the /OpenAction - and each address is listed once (1.5).
checks.documentInfo: Every non-empty entry of the trailer /Info dictionary counts - the standard Title, Author, Subject, Keywords and every non-standard (custom) key - EXCEPT /CreationDate, /ModDate and /Trapped, which never count, and /Creator and /Producer, which count only when the value is a file path (a drive path such as C:\..., a UNC path \\server\..., or an absolute POSIX path /...; a URL is not a path).
checks.onOpenFailure: When the file cannot be opened (open-failed), A9 also runs from the file's bytes, and these are EXPECTED, not optional: (1) the document information dictionary, under the documentInfo rule above - the LAST trailer's /Info reference, reading only that object's own bytes (a string inside a content stream is never read as a title), or a dictionary written inline in the trailer; (2) attachments - the presence of /EmbeddedFile, listed with their file names (/UF, else /F) when readable; (3) JavaScript - the presence of /JS or /S /JavaScript. Outlines, form values, comment text and hidden layers need the document's structure and are not expected from the bytes; the replacement texts are A8's (A8 onOpenFailure) (#113).

checks.title: 画像だけのページ
checks.rule: coverage = the sum, over all image paints on the page, of the area of each paint after CTM and the current clip path, intersected with the CropBox, divided by the CropBox area, capped at 1; review when there is no extractable text and coverage ≥ imageOnlyCoverage.
checks.$comment: Image paints are the images and image masks of the page content (not annotation appearances). Coverage never exceeds 1. A scan delivered as several strips is one scanned page (the strips add up); an image lying mostly off the CropBox counts only for the part on it (#105); two small images in opposite corners cover only their own area, not the box spanning them (#106). Overlapping paints are counted twice, which the cap at 1 bounds.

checks.title: 暗号化されていて検査できない
checks.rule: fires only when the file is encrypted and cannot be opened: not with the empty user password, nor with the password supplied. A file that opens (owner-password-only encryption, or the right password supplied) is examined like any other and does not raise A11.

recovered.$comment: text found under the cover. SCREEN ONLY: never written to a saved report, a log, or a file, by either implementation

detail.$comment: a short machine-readable code, never prose and never document text (no name, title, author, file name or recovered word). v1.2: it matches ^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$, with one exception: the detail of a page-not-examined finding is the failure name (a library's error type name such as InvalidOperationException, ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$). The failure name may instead be carried in evidence.failure (detail then a code); both conform, and a comparison never depends on which. Added after an implementation was found writing author names here. The saved report (JSON and text) must be byte-identical whether or not the findings carry recovered text

evidence.$comment: machine-comparable facts: coveredFraction, candidateSource, luminance, revisionIndex, ... Values are numbers, booleans or codes; a string value is a code or a standard PDF name (an annotation subtype, a replacement-text key), never document text (v1.2). Each string key has DECLARED values: a closed set (subtype: the ISO 32000-2 Table 171 names or other; colourSpace: the colour-space families or a fixed code such as unresolved or other; key: ActualText, Alt or E; ...) or the kind failure name (evidence.failure, ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$, a library's error type name). A name the document chose never passes through: a value outside the standard list is written as other. A string key an implementation has not declared is non-conformant; an implementation is expected to hold its declarations in one place and test every saved report against them

noteKey.$comment: v1.1: a fixed CODE, never prose, present only when the finding says something could not be examined (type3-not-inspected: a Type 3 glyph's drawing; fill-colour-unreadable: a shading or pattern cover; page-not-examined: an internal failure while examining the page, paired with checksSkipped check-failed, detail = the failure name; read-from-file-bytes: text read from the bytes of a file that could not be opened, which could not be compared with any page - an A7 earlier-revision text (A7 onOpenFailure) or an A8 replacement text (A8 onOpenFailure); earlier-revision-not-read (v1.2): A7 outcome 3, an earlier revision exists and nothing legible could be read from it, paired with checksSkipped revisions-not-readable, and the A7 finding of the chain floor when nothing at all could be read from the earlier bytes). See verdicts.wordingRules and verdicts.reviewFloor.

checksRun.$comment: the checks that ran, in check order (A1 ... A11); on open-failed that is A7, A8, A9 and A11

detail.$comment: a fixed machine name qualifying the code (a filter name, a library failure name); never prose, never document text

reasonCodes.file-too-large: the file exceeds the implementation's size limit
reasonCodes.password-required: encrypted, and neither the empty nor the supplied password opens it
reasonCodes.open-failed: the file could not be opened; detail = the library's failure name. Listed for the page checks (A1-A6, A10) only: A7, A8 and A9 still run from the file's bytes (checks.A7/A8/A9.onOpenFailure) and A11 runs, so those are in checksRun
reasonCodes.page-limit: only the first pages were examined; count = pages examined
reasonCodes.content-truncated: part of a page's content could not be read; page
reasonCodes.image-pixels-not-readable: an image's pixels could not be read; page, count, detail = the filter when known
reasonCodes.type3-glyph-not-inspected: Type 3 glyph procedures whose drawing was not inspected; page, count
reasonCodes.check-failed: an internal failure while examining that page; page, detail = the failure name. Never pass: the page carries a review finding with noteKey page-not-examined (verdicts.reviewFloor). Carried on A1 only (verdicts.pageLevelCarrier)
reasonCodes.revisions-not-readable: A7: earlier revisions that could not be read; detail chain (the cross-reference chain cannot be followed, or an %%EOF-marker prefix does not open) or revision (an earlier revision exists and nothing legible was read from it). Floors: verdicts.reviewFloor

notInspected.$comment: fixed KEYS, not sentences (v1.1); each surface shows its own localised sentence for a key. Keys: image-content-not-read (text drawn inside an image is not read), rescanned-paper-not-examinable (a printed-and-rescanned document cannot be examined beyond its images), completeness-not-judged (whether everything that should be blacked out was is not judged).

manifest.$comment: testdata/redaction-corpus/manifest.json: an object {specVersion, note, cases[]} (the browser checker's shape, adopted as is). Harnesses skip a case whose file is absent only when it is marked pending.
manifest.sharedExpectations: The manifest states what ANY conformant implementation must produce. Where implementations differ in capability (for example decompressing earlier revisions, #111), the shared expectation is the weaker of the two, and a check one of them may legitimately raise is in neither checks nor mustNotFlag. Implementations can differ by capability in either direction - one decompresses earlier revisions and the other does not (#111), one repairs a file that does not open as written and the other does not (#112) - so a case accepts what any conformant implementation must produce, and the stronger assertion each side can make lives in its own suite, as local, implementation-specific tests. A green shared run proves only what the manifest states.

verdict.$comment: the verdict of an implementation that decodes every image

checks.$comment: check ids that MUST be raised: a required subset (checksSemantics); others may be raised unless in mustNotFlag

mustNotFlag.$comment: check ids whose appearance is a false positive

acceptVerdicts.$comment: ONLY for capability-dependent cases: the verdicts accepted from an implementation that cannot decode the case's image (imageDecoding), or that repairs a file the other cannot open (#112). Must contain verdict, and may not add pass.

editorOnly.$comment: the browser checker may skip it; its verdict expectation still applies to the editor's checker

pending.$comment: the file is not in the corpus yet (e.g. needs Acrobat); harnesses report it as absent and skip it. A case whose file exists must not be pending.

madeBy.$comment: for source abyo-editor/acrobat: how the file was produced
